lead: twenty years in, the person closest to you would still guess wrong about how a thursday of yours goes. the visible half of your life has ended twice since you met. the other half nobody has seen.
sun: when the weather breaks here it takes what was on show, and what was on show was the whole of what anybody had. it does not reach the covered ground. that ground was never part of the life that ended, and nothing outside it had a route in, so the shedding costs it nothing, and the only ground in you that has come through every turning is ground nobody has been let into.
moon: the covering goes up before there is anything to conceal, around whatever is yours, without a decision. and it stands on one upright: one person has been inside since your twenties, from a life that ended a decade ago, and the whole interior is held by him. nothing has been added since. each new set of people arrives, is liked, and never once suspects there is ground.
pull: everything anybody has ever known about you has been shed at least twice. the part that has not altered since your twenties stands on one man, and he is owed.
tension: the woman you live with has worked out that there is a room she has not been in, and has assembled a reason for it: something in the life before this one, something that went wrong at the end. there is nothing in there. the account that would satisfy her requires opening the ground to somebody in a life that has not ended, and everything you have ever shown a current life has gone down with it.
cost: you have gone through total endings with your private week untouched, hour for hour, which is why they have never frightened you the way they frighten the people watching. there is one way in and one man who has ever used it. he is there on an obligation rather than a preference, and if he goes the covered ground does not become visible, it seals, with you inside it.

lead: your two lights sit fourteen stations apart, at opposite ends of the road, with nothing in between to bring them nearer: you build rooms meant to stand for thirty years, and you leave them completely.
sun: the break comes at full size and it is aimed at the season, never at the thing you built. you go out of the room absolutely, and the arrangement inside it stays exactly as designed, load for load, because nothing you make was ever holding you up. the people in it register a weather change and no structural one, which is accurate, and is also why none of them can date what happened.
moon: what you put up has an edge to it: a boundary, a load path, a settled question about who is inside. it holds by its geometry rather than by anybody's attendance, yours least of all, so your going takes nothing out of it. and nothing in you points at the corners afterwards. the rules that household runs on at breakfast were set by the one they describe as having left.
pull: the two ends of you never meet. what you build stands to outlast you, what you end is ended to the skin, and four people are dry tonight inside something you walked out of.
tension: at the table now it comes out as an accusation with evidence behind it: you arranged their whole life and then had no feeling about leaving it, and they learned you had gone from somebody else. the version that fits needs both facts held at their full separation, real construction and real ending, neither one a comment on the other, and produced out loud it sounds like claiming the walls on the way out of the door.
cost: the structures hold after you are out of them. arrangements usually need their maker in the room to keep standing, and none of yours has ever needed you in it. the distance runs the other way too. nothing you build is a place you can live, and what you still owe the people inside is paid across the width of the road, by somebody they no longer picture.

lead: you talked him into the work and he is nineteen years in and doing well. you left the same trade in one season, four years after him, and the two facts have never sat side by side for him.
sun: the trade stopped being anything to you inside one season and has not been thought about since, except when somebody rings. what the season did not touch is the directions. you would still walk a person in the same way tomorrow, past the same places where people turn round, and mean every word of it, which is the sentence they cannot get to sit beside the other one.
moon: the taking-across is the whole of the appetite, and it empties the moment the person is over. there is nothing in you for what comes after, no interest in their second decade. for once both halves of you want the same thing: you deliver and you go. what stays behind is one exact obligation to each of them, and never company.
pull: you are not on the road you put them on, and you would put them on it tomorrow. the route was true. it was finished in you before it was finished in them.
tension: one of them left the work the year after you did and said plainly that he had read your going as a verdict on it. putting him right would mean explaining, to somebody who has already resigned, that a season can finish inside one person and mean nothing about the road. so you tell him the work is good, and the ones still in it watch you for the next sign and take your silence as the second one.
cost: a person gets the whole route from you, including the parts somebody usually holds something of, because you have nothing in it left to protect and no plan to be there when they arrive. what nobody gets is a second stretch. the ones you brought across write to a person finished with the country they live in, and the answers go out promptly with no questions in them.

lead: the oldest thing running in your life is a line you tied before the rest of it existed. everything else has ended whole, more than once. out of each ending came one length, and you have kept every one tight.
sun: an ending here is where the choosing happens. the season closes, everything in it goes at the same rate, and the last act of the whole business is the tying-off: one arrangement gets carried out of a life that has otherwise stopped existing. you have never argued with yourself about which. by the time the weather changes it has already been settled, and everything not on the list goes without a hearing.
moon: your end of each length moves every few years and the far ends do not move at all. the strain of that is taken up entirely on your side, weekly: the money moving before it is asked for, the drive out at the end of a bad week. and when a far end lets go, you feel the slack immediately, and nothing in your own completeness reaches that far.
pull: the lives are gone; the lengths are not. when you go, nothing will record them — they will drop, and each person at the far end will lose a thing that never had a name.
tension: the ones who arrived late watch you drive four hours for a person who cannot name your job, and settle on guilt: something must have happened at that ending, and this is the instalment plan. nothing happened. the going was clean, and the length is kept tight for no reason beyond its being yours to keep, which leaves you explaining a mechanism to people who came for a confession, and giving up halfway through, every time.
cost: nobody is left waiting to find out which they were. the sorting happens in the week the season closes, and the ones let go know it, and the one carried out knows it. what follows is written down nowhere. one grip holds it, and the day the grip goes everything taken out of every ending drops together, and each far end is told it was age.
